notes: Promoted by hand from the `tools/tubuild.py promote --dry-run` plan (promote is dry-run only). 36 of the class's 55 shards are folded in; the source's own header comment carries the reconciliation notes.

THE DESTRUCTOR PAIR IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, AND NOT FOR THE USUAL REASON. The cartridge orders them D1 (0x0211f000) then D0 (0x0211f0a0), which is the REPRODUCIBLE direction -- measured here on mwccarm 2004/b56, an inline in-class `virtual ~daKuriKing_c() {}` emits the pair with no D2, while an out-of-line definition emits D2 (0xa0), D0 (0xb4), D1 (0xa0) in that section order. The blocker is the KEY FUNCTION. With the destructor inline the key function becomes the first out-of-line virtual the class declares, Behavior at 0x02121bf0, which is on the far side of the near-miss hole. A TU that does not own the key function emits no vtable, and with no vtable nothing odr-uses the destructor, so neither variant is emitted at all (measured: a probe TU over the inline-destructor header emits zero symbols beyond its own function). A forcing scaffold does emit the pair, and in ROM order when `delete p;` precedes `p->~daKuriKing_c();` -- the variants come out in reverse order of first odr-use, measured here and recorded in no role file -- but mwccarm emits the scaffold itself into .text immediately BELOW D1, and D1 sits at 0x0211f000, the first byte of ov074's .text. There is no address below it. src/_ZN12daKuriKing_cD1Ev.cpp and src/_ZN12daKuriKing_cD0Ev.cpp therefore keep their own delinks entries and this object emits no copy of either.

THE ONE THING BETWEEN 36 AND 55 IS func_ov074_02121380. Match it and the hole closes, a single TU owns Behavior and therefore the key function, the vtable and both destructors come with it, and the whole 0x0211f000..0x0212290c run promotes. notes/mwccarm-codegen.md 6bq records the levers already tried and calls it one lever short.

The manifest is text-only. _ZTV12daKuriKing_c (ov074:0x02122eb8, 31 slots, 0x7c symbol extent / 0x84 storage) and the whole dEnemyBase_c -> dActor_c -> dBase_c -> fBase_c vague-linkage chain are NOT emitted by this object at all, because the licensed range excludes the key function; there is nothing to deadstrip but Vector3's inline destructor. `externalized_output` is absent -- no symbol needed the canonical-import route.

The row count was MEASURED, not inherited: ov074 had no sibling oracle. A probe TU that owns the key function emits exactly 11 data symbols -- _ZTV12daKuriKing_c plus _ZTI/_ZTS for daKuriKing_c, dEnemyBase_c, dActor_c, dBase_c and fBase_c -- which is 2 x 5 levels + 1 vtable, the formula's prediction, exact. This entry needs 1 row rather than 11 only because its licensed range excludes the key function.

NOTE FOR THE NEXT ov074 WRITER, REVISED BY THE RENAME. This entry used to warn that a TU owning the key function would emit _ZTI8Goomboss and _ZTS8Goomboss under the coined name, and that romdata_check.check_object would report both UNNAMED because the cartridge homes those addresses as _ZTI12daKuriKing_c / _ZTS12daKuriKing_c -- which is why those two rows were plain `deadstrip` (homeless) rather than `deadstrip-data`. That trap is GONE. The class now carries its cartridge name, so a key-function TU emits _ZTV12daKuriKing_c, _ZTI12daKuriKing_c and _ZTS12daKuriKing_c, and all three are homed by ov074's symbols.txt. All eleven rows are therefore deadstrip-data with canonical addresses: _ZTV12daKuriKing_c ov074:0x02122eb8, _ZTI12daKuriKing_c ov074:0x02122e30, _ZTS12daKuriKing_c ov074:0x02122e3c, _ZTI12dEnemyBase_c ov002:0x021081c0, _ZTS12dEnemyBase_c ov002:0x021081cc, _ZTI8dActor_c arm9:0x0208e390, _ZTS8dActor_c arm9:0x0208e384, _ZTI7dBase_c arm9:0x02086e78, _ZTS7dBase_c arm9:0x02086e54, _ZTI7fBase_c arm9:0x02086d70, _ZTS7fBase_c arm9:0x02086e60.
